headline_marked: [[Crusoe raises $3.9B]] in Series F, valuing AI infrastructure firm at $30.9B
headline: Crusoe raises $3.9B in Series F, valuing AI infrastructure firm at $30.9B
summary: The massive Series F round pushes Crusoe's valuation to $30.9 billion. The capital will fund existing data centers, including one for OpenAI, and new truck-transportable modular 'AI factories'.
details: AI infrastructure developer Crusoe has announced a colossal $3.9 billion Series F funding round, elevating its valuation to $30.9 billion. This massive investment was co-led by Atreides Management, Mubadala Capital, and Valor Equity Partners, with participation from major players like Nvidia and Founders Fund.

The company also welcomed three new board members, including Cloudflare CFO Thomas Seifert and Redwood Materials founder JB Straubel. Straubel, a Tesla board member, previously invested in Crusoe and saw them become Redwood's first energy storage customer.

This fresh capital infusion will finance Crusoe's existing data center projects, notably a large site in Abilene, Texas, utilized by OpenAI. It will also support the development of smaller, modular 'Spark' AI factories designed for truck transport and quick connection to power sources.

By manufacturing these modular units in-house, Crusoe can rapidly deploy compute capacity without extensive construction workforces. These smaller centers also help mitigate local community backlash often associated with large data center complexes.

Crusoe co-founder and CEO Chase Lochmiller stated his belief that achieving an era of AI abundance requires 'controlling the infrastructure from electrons to tokens.' He expressed gratitude for investors who share this conviction.

The company's revenue streams include leasing data center space to customers with their own GPUs, renting out its own GPUs, and selling compute power for AI model inference. This diversified model has made Crusoe a leading AI infrastructure firm.

Crusoe recently secured a substantial $13 billion, five-year cloud contract to provide GPUs and AI infrastructure to quantitative trading firm Jane Street. Discussions with investment bankers suggest a potential IPO in the near future.

Founded in 2018 as a crypto mining operation, Crusoe pivoted to AI infrastructure as demand for computing power surged. The company's customer base now includes tech giants like Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle.

headline_marked: Apple [[pushes UK court to lift secrecy]] around encryption backdoor order
headline: Apple pushes UK court to lift secrecy around encryption backdoor order
summary: Apple is challenging the UK government's refusal to confirm if it issued an order for access to encrypted user data, aiming for transparency on potential encryption backdoors.
details: Apple has initiated legal action against the UK government, challenging its decision to keep secret any orders demanding access to encrypted user data. The tech giant seeks to compel the government to publicly disclose whether it has issued such a directive.

This move comes as Apple aims to ensure transparency regarding potential encryption backdoors that could compromise user privacy. The company believes the public has a right to know if their data is being accessed by state authorities without explicit confirmation.

The case highlights ongoing tensions between tech companies and governments over data privacy and national security. Apple has historically taken a strong stance on end-to-end encryption and user data protection.

A public confirmation would clarify the scope of government powers under existing legislation and its impact on encrypted services. This legal battle could set a precedent for how governments interact with tech firms on matters of digital privacy.
